title.full: ASEAN Green Future Project Phase 2.1 & 2.2 Report, Modeling Myanmar's path to a Near-Zero Emissions Power sector by 2050

publisher.full: Sustainable Development Solutions Network and ClimateWorks Centre

description: Myanmar-specific cost-optimized pathway following current energy policies and NDCs.

coreDrivers.policies: "Demand side sector energy demand follows Myanmar official targets. To fulfil this demand, the optimisation tool NEMO was utilised to determine the least-cost generation mix while ensuring a reserve margin above 30% at all times".
coreDrivers.technologyCosts: Technology capital, O&M and fuel costs affect least-cost capacity choices; falling solar and battery costs support deployment.
coreDrivers.macroeconomicDrivers: SSP2 GDP, medium population growth extracted from World Bank and sectoral value-added trends from country target drive electricity demand.
coreDrivers.otherDrivers: A >30% reserve-margin constraint is a key design driver.

dependencies.dependency_description: National targets shapes power generation demand. A least cost approach is added to determine capacity additions.
The scenario’s power technology mix retains meaningful exposure to natural gas, increasing its vulnerability to gas price volatility and potential supply disruptions.
Local opposition to large hydropower already stricked in Myanmar. This scenario doesn't forecast any addition in hydropower.
Consumer and client are assumed to follow Myanmar power demand target.

OEPP is built with same scenario ambition than Existing Policy Scenario but capacity additions are based on least cost optimization and power grid system needs to maintain reserve margin at a safe level above 30%.
Battery storage plays an important role in the OEPP scenario, reaching an installed capacity of 1.47 GW by 2050.
OEPP remains exposed to domestic gas and LNG supply constraints and price volatility. Its plateau in hydropower capacity, however, keeps incremental exposure to drought-related risks relatively low.
Drought and climate variability threaten hydropower reliability.
